html:
Jonestown was the jungle settlement of the Peoples Temple, an American religious group led by Jim Jones, in northwest Guyana. On 18 November 1978 more than 900 of its people died there in a mass murder and suicide by poison, and four more at the Temple's house in Georgetown.

Jones had moved his followers from California to Guyana in the 1970s, with the approval of the government of Forbes Burnham. Relatives complained that members were held against their will. A United States congressman, Leo Ryan, came to see. As his party left from the airstrip at Port Kaituma, gunmen from the settlement killed him and four others.

That evening Jones ordered his followers to drink a poisoned fruit drink. Over 300 of the dead were children. It became a byword worldwide for the dangers of cults, and in Guyana it shamed a government that had let the settlement run unchecked.
